To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

security policies for BPEL-based cross-domain business processes can be assessed prior to execution and that this can be achieved by specifying security policies with regard to security-relevant semantics in BPEL.
security policies can be specified with respect to semantic patterns in BPL and that these policies can be used to check the security compliance of BPEL-based business processes prior to execution.
a method to specify and assess security policies with respect security-relevant semantic aspects of BPEL processes is applicable in the Grid context with minor modifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of methods for the specification of security policies with respect security-relevant semantic aspects of Grid processes and the assessment of such policies for compliance with security requirements.
the following questions: (i) How can the security-relevant semantics for BPEL-based cross-domain processes be formalized?
the development of a methodology for the specification of security policies for BPEL-based processes and their enforcement by means of an appropriate security infrastructure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the results of our research are not transferable to the Grid context, but that they are applicable for a limited subset of Grid applications, namely those where the security policies are similar to the ones used for cooperative business processes.
the results of the research project are transferable to the Grid context with respect to the assessment of security policies of remotely defined BPL-based Grid processes prior to execution.
the method for security policy assessment of remotely defined Grid processes is applicable, but requires further research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a transfer to Grid computing is possible, but that further research on the security semantics of Grid services is required.
we were able to transfer the results of the former research to the field of grid computing.
the transfer was successful for cooperative Grid processes, whereas for the general Grid context the situation is still unclear.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the approach for security policy enforcement for cooperative processes can be transferred to Grid processes.
security policy enforcement in Grid environments is a challenging task and that further research is necessary to make it feasible in the near future.

the method is suitable to support the security assessment of BPEL-based processes in general, and that it can also be applied to Grid computing, provided that the security requirements are similar to those in cooperative business processes.
